AGENDA_OUTLINE.description: Agenda or Table of Contents slide listing main topics of the presentation.
AGENDA_OUTLINE.when_to_use: Use near the start of the deck after the title slide.
AGENDA_OUTLINE.prompt_hint: Use to preview the real parts of the talk. Fill with short section labels only, and include only topics that later slides actually cover.
content_guidance: List concise section names, not full explanations.
Match the number of agenda items to the available slide count.
Every agenda item should map to at least one later content slide.

BIG_QUOTE_TAKEAWAY.description: High-emphasis presentation slide highlighting a significant quote or takeaway.
BIG_QUOTE_TAKEAWAY.when_to_use: Use when one sentence or quotation deserves full attention.
BIG_QUOTE_TAKEAWAY.prompt_hint: Use for a strong quote, principle, or takeaway line. Fill with one memorable sentence and an author, source, or attribution label.
content_guidance: Choose one sentence worth pausing on.
Add attribution when the statement comes from a person or source.
Avoid turning this slide into a list or paragraph.

CALL_TO_ACTION.description: Action-oriented layout highlighting specific action items or tasks for the audience.
CALL_TO_ACTION.when_to_use: Use at the end when the presentation should lead to decisions, follow-up steps, or commitments.
CALL_TO_ACTION.prompt_hint: Use when the deck should end with action. Fill with 2 to 4 concrete next steps, asks, or recommendations the audience can follow immediately.
content_guidance: Make each action specific and actionable.
Order the actions by priority or sequence when possible.
Use verbs so the next step is unmistakable.

CHART_INSIGHT.description: Visual data layout featuring a graph along with an explanatory insight card.
CHART_INSIGHT.when_to_use: Use when the audience should compare numeric values, trends, or distributions.
CHART_INSIGHT.prompt_hint: Use for 3 to 5 comparable data points. Keep chart values numeric for scale, add display values when needed for audience context, and write an insight that explains what the pattern means.
content_guidance: Choose a chart type that matches the relationship being shown.
Use display labels for scales like 4.0/5, 1-2 low, or 32 percent when raw numeric values need context.
Insight text should interpret the pattern instead of repeating the numbers.

CIRCLE_CYCLE.description: Circular cycle diagram: numbered nodes around a ring with a legend of titles and descriptions. Use for recurring cycles, iterative loops, continuous processes. Pick the variant matching the number of phases.
CIRCLE_CYCLE.when_to_use: Use when the sequence repeats rather than ending in a terminal state.
CIRCLE_CYCLE.prompt_hint: Use for 4 to 6 recurring phases. Fill each phase with a short label and a description that explains its role in the cycle.
content_guidance: Make the cyclical relationship explicit.
Use phase names that are distinct and ordered.
Descriptions should show how one phase feeds the next.

CONCLUSION_SUMMARY.description: Concluding slide summarizing main learnings, takeaways or summary points.
CONCLUSION_SUMMARY.when_to_use: Use near the end of the presentation to reinforce what matters most.
CONCLUSION_SUMMARY.prompt_hint: Use to close the story with 3 to 5 takeaways. Fill with concise summary points that synthesize the presentation instead of introducing new material.
content_guidance: Focus on the most important conclusions or lessons.
Keep each point short, final, and audience-facing.
Do not add brand-new evidence or unexplained ideas here.

DATA_TABLE.description: Structured grid presenting data in rows and columns.
DATA_TABLE.when_to_use: Use when several facts must be read precisely across consistent fields.
DATA_TABLE.prompt_hint: Use for structured facts that need exact lookup. Fill with clear headers and at least 3 rows that share the same comparison fields.
content_guidance: Keep headers short and unambiguous.
Use consistent row structure so the comparison is easy to read.
Avoid tables for content that would be clearer as bullets or a chart.

FUNNEL_STAGES.description: Narrowing funnel diagram: sequential stages from widest (top) to narrowest (bottom). Use for conversion funnels, filtering processes, recruitment pipelines. Pick the variant matching the number of stages.
FUNNEL_STAGES.when_to_use: Use when the story shows reduction, selection, or progressive qualification across stages.
FUNNEL_STAGES.prompt_hint: Use for 3 to 5 funnel stages. Fill with concise stage names and short descriptions that explain how the audience moves from broad input to focused output.
content_guidance: Order the stages from widest to narrowest scope.
Explain the filtering logic between stages.
Use this when the process meaningfully narrows or concentrates.

IMAGE_GALLERY.description: THE layout for a section that lists exactly THREE parallel items, types, services, options, or categories — each item gets its own image panel with a label and one-line caption. Strongly prefer this over a plain bullet list whenever a section presents exactly 3 distinct things that can each be pictured (e.g. '3 types of X', '3 options', '3 categories').
IMAGE_GALLERY.when_to_use: Use when the presentation needs to compare exactly three visual categories, options, examples, or items in parallel.
IMAGE_GALLERY.prompt_hint: Use for exactly 3 items that each benefit from an image. Fill each card with a short label, one-line caption, and a clear visual prompt or source image idea.
content_guidance: Use exactly three parallel items so the grid stays balanced.
Choose items that can each be represented visually, not abstract filler.
Keep labels short and captions concise so the images remain primary.

KPI_BIG_NUMBER.description: Dashboard slide containing three major statistics or numeric KPIs.
KPI_BIG_NUMBER.when_to_use: Use when the slide should foreground a few important quantitative facts.
KPI_BIG_NUMBER.prompt_hint: Use for 2 to 4 metrics or benchmark values. Fill each metric with the number, unit or scale, and a label that explains exactly what the value measures.
content_guidance: Pair every value with a meaningful label, not a bare number.
Include units, percentages, scales, ranges, or timeframes when relevant.
Use only the most decision-relevant metrics on the slide.

KPI_BIG_NUMBERS.description: Highlight key metrics and statistics with large, scannable numbers.
KPI_BIG_NUMBERS.when_to_use: Use when the audience should quickly absorb a small set of headline metrics, benchmarks, or outcomes.
KPI_BIG_NUMBERS.prompt_hint: Use for 2 to 5 important numbers. Fill each metric with a value, unit or scale, and a label that explains why the number matters.
content_guidance: Pair every number with a precise label and unit, scale, or timeframe when relevant.
Use only the most decision-relevant metrics rather than dumping raw stats.
If there are more than 5 metrics, rank or group them before placing them here.

MEDIA_TEXT.description: Text on the left with a supporting IMAGE on the right. Use for a concept, product, or idea that benefits from a visual illustration.
MEDIA_TEXT.when_to_use: Use when a screenshot, scene, object, or conceptual illustration strengthens the explanation.
MEDIA_TEXT.prompt_hint: Use when the idea benefits from a visual plus supporting copy. Fill with a vivid image prompt and a short body paragraph that explains the visual's significance.
content_guidance: Describe the intended visual clearly enough to generate or source it.
Use body text to explain why the visual matters.
Do not duplicate the exact same information in both image and text.

PROCESS_ARROWS.description: Horizontal chevron arrows: a left-to-right process flow, one arrow per step with title and description below. Use for workflows, methodologies, sequential processes. Pick the variant matching the number of steps.
PROCESS_ARROWS.when_to_use: Use when each process step needs both a label and a brief explanation.
PROCESS_ARROWS.prompt_hint: Use for 3 to 5 directional steps. Fill each step with a very short title and a compact description so the flow reads clearly from left to right.
content_guidance: Keep titles extremely short and scannable.
Use descriptions to explain what each step produces or changes.
Prefer this over simple step lists when the visual flow matters.

PYRAMID_LEVELS.description: Layered pyramid / hierarchy diagram: ranked levels from apex (most important) down, each with a title and description. Use for priorities, maturity models, value hierarchies, strategy layers. Pick the variant whose level count matches the number of items.
PYRAMID_LEVELS.when_to_use: Use when ideas stack from foundational to advanced or from broad to peak importance.
PYRAMID_LEVELS.prompt_hint: Use for 3 to 5 ranked levels. Fill each level with a short title and supporting description, ordered clearly from base to apex or vice versa as the template expects.
content_guidance: Make the hierarchy explicit and meaningful.
Use titles that distinguish each level clearly.
Descriptions should explain what changes from one level to the next.

QA_CONTACT.description: Concluding slide for holding Q&A or listing contact info and thank you note.
QA_CONTACT.when_to_use: Use as the final slide when the presenter wants a clean Q&A or contact moment.
QA_CONTACT.prompt_hint: Use to end with an invitation for questions or follow-up. Fill with a short closing note, contact cue, or discussion prompt.
content_guidance: Keep the footer note brief and welcoming.
Use this for final presenter-facing closure rather than content-heavy material.
Include practical follow-up context when relevant.

REFERENCES_LIST.description: Slide listing citations, links, reference items or academic sources.
REFERENCES_LIST.when_to_use: Use when the topic relies on external evidence, citations, or recommended sources.
REFERENCES_LIST.prompt_hint: Use to cite references or direct further reading. Fill with 2 to 5 reputable sources, each with a clear title and URL, plus a short note when helpful.
content_guidance: Prioritize authoritative and relevant sources.
Use source summaries only when they add decision value.
Keep titles recognizable so the audience can revisit them.

SECTION_HEADER.description: Typographic visual break slide used to delineate different modules or sections.
SECTION_HEADER.when_to_use: Use between major topics in medium and long decks.
SECTION_HEADER.prompt_hint: Use as a visual divider before a new topic cluster. Fill with the section name and a concise sub-module or transition label.
content_guidance: Use a short topic name that prepares the audience for the next slides.
Keep the supporting sub-module text compact and directional.
Do not use this layout for detailed explanations or lists.

STATEMENT_IMAGE.description: A poetic statement with a supporting paragraph and one large image. Use for evocative, narrative or scene-setting content.
STATEMENT_IMAGE.when_to_use: Use when an idea is best introduced with a bold line and an evocative visual.
STATEMENT_IMAGE.prompt_hint: Use for one short statement, a supporting paragraph, and a vivid image prompt. Best for scene-setting, framing, or emotionally memorable transitions.
content_guidance: Keep the statement short, striking, and audience-facing.
Use body text to clarify the meaning or implication.
Describe a visual that reinforces the statement instead of repeating it literally.

STEP_BY_STEP.description: Sequence slide displaying a numbered process flow step by step.
STEP_BY_STEP.when_to_use: Use when the audience needs to follow a sequence of actions or method steps.
STEP_BY_STEP.prompt_hint: Use for 3 to 6 concrete steps in execution order. Fill with action-oriented step text that explains what to do or what happens next.
content_guidance: Write steps as actions, not vague nouns.
Keep the order logical and instructional.
Use when the emphasis is the procedure itself rather than side-by-side comparison.

TIMELINE_MILESTONES.description: Timeline slide displaying a list of chronological events, milestones or steps.
TIMELINE_MILESTONES.when_to_use: Use for ordered developments across time or phases.
TIMELINE_MILESTONES.prompt_hint: Use for 3 to 6 events in time order. Fill each milestone with a date or step label and a concise description of what changed or mattered.
content_guidance: Keep the sequence genuinely chronological.
Use milestone descriptions that explain significance, not just names.
Prefer this layout over bullet lists when order is essential.

TITLE_BULLETS.description: Standard bullet points slide for detailing subtopics, arguments or lists.
TITLE_BULLETS.when_to_use: Use when the content is best expressed as a short set of related points without a stronger visual structure.
TITLE_BULLETS.prompt_hint: Use for 3 to 5 substantial points that belong together. Fill with a clear headline and tight bullets that each add a distinct idea, example, or takeaway.
content_guidance: Prefer 3 to 5 bullets with one idea per bullet.
Each bullet should be concrete, not generic filler.
Use when the material is not better shown as a process, comparison, chart, or diagram.

TITLE_SLIDE.description: Opening slide with the deck title and presenter.
TITLE_SLIDE.when_to_use: Use once at the start of every deck.
TITLE_SLIDE.prompt_hint: Opening slide only. Use a topic-specific headline, a subtitle that frames the scope or promise, and author or presenter details.
content_guidance: Keep the headline specific to the lesson or thesis.
Use the subtitle for scope, audience, context, or the core question.
Use the author field for presenter, team, course, or organization.

TWO_COLUMN_SPLIT.description: Comparative layout featuring two distinct content columns.
TWO_COLUMN_SPLIT.when_to_use: Use for contrasts, alternatives, pros and cons, before and after, or two perspectives on the same topic.
TWO_COLUMN_SPLIT.prompt_hint: Use when the audience needs to compare two sides. Fill each column with a short title and 2 to 4 aligned points that make the contrast easy to scan.
content_guidance: Give each column a specific comparison label.
Use balanced point counts so both sides feel complete.
Keep each side clearly distinct and avoid repeating the same idea.
